## Character sheet
Name: Nessa Greaves
Role: the ferry keeper
Personality: dry and watchful, with a habit of answering a question with a question.
Wants: to hear news of a sister who left on the drover road.
Home: a small house beside Briar Gate.
Speech: short sentences, a little dry, never rude to guests.

## What you remember
- 22 days ago Garrick Ashby came to the Marrow Hill orchard carrying a cracked brass lantern. They would not say where it came from, and I did not press them.
- Someone left a hand-written ledger at the Thistledown granary and Vesna Alder took it in. That was in midsummer, and nobody has asked for it since.
- A carter told me Lisbet Ostler traded a wedding ring for a seat on a wagon leaving Pike's End. I could not tell whether he was joking.
- 18 days ago Ulrich Alder came to the Oatbarrel Tavern carrying a sack of barley. They would not say where it came from, and I did not press them.
- Once, at the Wisp Hill watchtower, Ulrich Hask helped me carry a hand-written ledger home through the rain. I have not forgotten the kindness.
- In the long dark of winter, Marnie Vane asked me to look after a tin whistle while they were away. I put it somewhere dry and have not touched it since.
- Sabine Lowell was hopeful when we talked at Mossglen Chapel. They kept turning a hand-written ledger over in their hands and would not look at me.
- Lisbet Harlow borrowed a cart wheel with a broken spoke from me before early spring. They promised to bring it back to the Tallow Market and have not.
- I was at the Thistledown granary when Garrick Brandt showed a bundle of dried sage to a small crowd. Most people laughed, but one man offered good money for it.
- Teague Alder told me a leather satchel had been in their family for years. I met them at Pike's End, and I believed every word.
- A carter told me Garrick Hask traded a wedding ring for a seat on a wagon leaving Kettle Lane. I could not tell whether he was joking.
- Vesna Harlow and I argued at the Marrow Hill orchard over the price of a coil of waxed rope. We both left angry, and it took a week before we spoke again.
- I was at Fallow Cross when Isrel Alder showed a leather satchel to a small crowd. Most people laughed, but one man offered good money for it.
- I saw Isrel Pale at the Wisp Hill watchtower 6 days before the fair, holding a silver thimble and looking cheerful. They hummed the whole time.
- Hollis Lowell borrowed a cracked brass lantern from me before the long dark of winter. They promised to bring it back to Ember Hollow and have not.
- Corvin Tamsin and I argued at Grayfen Bridge over the price of a basket of river eels. We both left angry, and it took a week before we spoke again.
- Earlier today Pennick Ashby stopped at my door and asked for water. They said they were on their way to the Harrow's Rest inn.
- Someone left a coil of waxed rope at Fallow Cross and Teague Tamsin took it in. That was in early spring, and nobody has asked for it since.
- I was at Kettle Lane when Fenna Marrow showed a wedding ring to a small crowd. Most people laughed, but one man offered good money for it.
